content:
A 111th District Court judge has sentenced 21-year-old Alizza Monique Scribner to two years of probation for child endangerment, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The sentence closes a case that began in May 2024, when a 2-year-old child was found unattended in an empty lot near Scribner's home.

According to the report, the toddler was found by a neighbor at about 12:10 a.m. on May 11, 2024, in the 2900 block of East Stewart Street, roughly 75 yards from Scribner's residence. Scribner had been searching for the child but had not called 911 during that search, the report said.

Scribner initially pleaded not guilty in early 2026, then changed her plea to guilty on July 29, 2026, according to the report. The court sentenced her on Oct. 13, 2026, imposing a formal sentence rather than deferred adjudication. As part of the sentence, she must complete 100 hours of community service and a parenting class.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, “Laredo woman gets probation after child found alone in empty lot,” Oct. 2026.

title: Laredo woman sentenced to probation in child endangerment case
